description: Operation-level agent capability registry. This file is the single machine-readable answer to one question: which Factory operations may an autonomous task ever reach, and under what policy. An internal Factory HTTP route existing is not an answer to that question. `apps/service/src/tool-contract.js` remains the service transport contract; this registry is the narrower agent-facing surface projected from it, and `packages/control-plane/src/capabilities.js` is the code that enforces it before dispatch.
rules: Deny-by-default. An operation absent from `capabilities` is not agent-reachable, whatever HTTP route serves it.

A capability is granted to a role only when the role's policy allows every entry in `requiredPolicyActions` outright and the role's declared mutationScopes cover every entry in `requiredMutationScopes`. Owning some mutation scope never grants every mutating operation.

A role that owns no mutation scope at all receives no mutating operation, including one that writes no project file. Making the projection granular must only narrow it: a reviewer must not gain an operation the coarse mutating/non-mutating split withheld.
This registry may be stricter than the service tool contract and never laxer: an operation the contract marks approvalRequired must be approvalRequired here too, or absent.
`approvalRequired` is executable. The trusted broker refuses the operation unless the signed grant carries a matching, unexpired approval for the same operation and project.

`internalOnlyOperations` and `internalOnlyRoutes` are the explicit record of the rich internal surface that exists for the Builder Console and must never become an agent operation. `marker` is the literal fragment of `apps/service/src/http.js` that serves the route, so the declaration is tested against a real consumer rather than trusted as prose.

capabilities.reason: Enumerating durable projects is read-only Factory state.
Reading one project's durable record is read-only Factory state.
The Project Manifest is task context every role may need.
The knowledge pack is trusted factory-owned data with instructionAuthority none.
The ingested-source inventory is provenance a role must be able to check.
Composition output is deterministic factory state.
Reading current content overrides is required before proposing a change to them.
Durable task state is how a fresh session reconstructs its next action.
The event ledger is the durable record a resumed attempt reads.
Metrics are aggregate factory state, not a control operation.
Resuming from the latest checkpoint requires reading it.
Checkpoint history is read-only recovery context.
Preview status is a read of factory-owned runtime state.
Configured/not-configured status carries no secret value.
Creating a durable project is a write, so a read-only role must not reach it. It touches no existing project workspace, so it needs no file mutation scope.
Content overrides change what the generated application renders from src/**. A role that does not own src/** may read them and may not write them.
Generation rewrites the project's source and public assets, so it needs both scopes and the ability to build.
Verification writes durable task and event state but no project source, so it is bounded by process policy rather than by file scope.
Starting a bounded preview process is a build-class operation, not a source mutation.
Stopping a preview is the reverse of starting one and carries the same class.
Ingestion is the one operation that causes outbound requests and admits new material into the durable knowledge pack. It is approval-gated for an agent even though the Console may run it directly.

internalOnlyOperations.reason: Source governance decides whether crawled material may inform the knowledge pack. That is a human/Console trust decision about untrusted content, and an agent that could make it could launder its own instructions into factory-trusted state.

Listing a project's approved build plans exposes which generations an operator has already authorised. It backs the Console approval screen; an agent that could read it learns nothing it needs and gains a map of the approval boundary.
Reading one approved plan returns the frozen project-state fingerprint an execution will be checked against. Console only, for the same reason as the list.

Approval is the explicit local operator confirmation the whole boundary rests on. An agent that could approve could authorise its own generation, which is precisely the authority this contract exists to withhold.

Execution spends an approval an operator made. Until there is an approved policy for who may spend one, the operator who minted the plan is the only actor allowed to redeem it; a later integration may execute plans already approved inside App Builder, and that grant belongs in the change that makes it.
